title: Profile and summary
text: Huining Li is a Technical Lead and the sole founder of ShuttleRise, based in Brisbane, Australia. He is an Australian citizen. His background is in lending, payments and full-stack software, and his core stack is .NET, Azure, TypeScript and AI engineering. From February 2023 to August 2026 he was Technical Lead at Fsoft, leading six engineers on a multi-tenant lending and payments platform while remaining 40-50% hands-on across .NET, Azure and Angular, and shipping production AI services. Since March 2026 he has been building ShuttleRise, an independent React, Node.js and PostgreSQL product, using AI coding agents. He has worked as a software engineer in Brisbane since July 2012.

title: Founder of ShuttleRise (March 2026 to present)
text: Since March 2026 Huining has been the sole founder and developer of ShuttleRise (shuttlerise.com), an independent venture building a platform for badminton clubs. He owns product direction, architecture and full-stack delivery. He built the React/TypeScript frontend, Node.js/Express APIs and PostgreSQL data layer using AI coding agents under his direction, with Claude Code and Codex in the development workflow. Features include separate player, club and admin roles, event registration, singles and doubles draw generation, Bayesian player ratings and durable background result processing. He built Stripe payment and refund workflows with webhook processing, retry controls and recovery handling, and integrated authentication (including Google sign-in), email via Resend, product analytics via PostHog and error monitoring via Sentry. Automated UI and API tests back it up, including integration checks against disposable PostgreSQL databases. The source code is private; the tech stack is listed publicly on StackShare. ShuttleRise is an independent venture rather than an employer with staff, and it overlapped with his final months at Fsoft.

title: ShuttleRise tech stack
text: ShuttleRise's tech stack, which is also listed publicly at stackshare.io/hiro.l.dragon/shuttlerise. Frontend: React 18, Vite and strict TypeScript, with shadcn/ui components on Radix UI, Tailwind CSS, React Router, React Hook Form with Zod validation, Recharts for charts and the Socket.IO client for real-time updates. Backend: Node.js, Express and strict TypeScript, with PostgreSQL accessed through the pg driver using raw SQL rather than an ORM, Passport.js for email and Google sign-in with JWT sessions in HttpOnly cookies, OpenAPI contracts shared between frontend and backend, Zod and Ajv request validation, Helmet and rate limiting, Pino structured logging and node-cron scheduled jobs. Integrations: Stripe for payments and refunds, Resend for email, PostHog for product analytics and Sentry for error monitoring. Testing and tooling: Vitest, Testing Library, Supertest, MSW, automated accessibility checks, Playwright end-to-end tests and integration tests against disposable PostgreSQL databases, in an npm workspaces monorepo with ESLint, Prettier and GitHub Actions CI. Development uses Claude Code and Codex as AI coding agents.

title: Technical Lead at Fsoft (February 2023 to August 2026)
text: Huining was Technical Lead at Fsoft Pty Ltd in Brisbane from February 2023 to August 2026, after joining as a Senior Software Engineer in July 2020. He led six engineers on BizCore, a multi-tenant lending and payments platform, while spending roughly 40-50% of his time hands-on across .NET, Azure and Angular. His remit combined architecture and technical direction, design and code reviews, people leadership including mentoring and performance reviews, and infrastructure. He defined the Azure infrastructure in Bicep and connected it to CI/CD, designed blue/green releases behind Azure Front Door, built and shipped a Node.js/TypeScript RAG service with MCP endpoints, introduced Claude Code and Codex to the team, led Azure AI Search customer matching, and led the frontend migration to Angular 20+ with signals. Across his two Fsoft roles he also led the platform's migration from .NET Framework to .NET 8.

title: Senior Software Engineer at Fsoft (July 2020 to February 2023)
text: From July 2020 to February 2023 Huining was a Senior Software Engineer at Fsoft Pty Ltd in Brisbane. He led development of BizCore, a loan management and payment processing platform for private lenders in Australia and New Zealand, across the loan lifecycle: origination, assessment, servicing, payment collection and maturity. He built direct-debit and recurring-payment processing, along with features supporting SACC and MACC consumer-lending requirements. He also built a customer portal for web and mobile that lets borrowers manage their loans. The work spanned C#, .NET, Angular, SQL Server and Azure, with Entity Framework Core, MediatR and domain-driven design.

title: BizCore platform: scale and domain
text: BizCore, the lending and payments platform Huining worked on at Fsoft, serves 250,000+ loans and 600,000+ customer records. It operates under Australian financial-services regulation, including SACC and MACC consumer credit rules, so customer-data isolation, careful handling of personal information, auditability and compliance controls are designed in from the start rather than added later. The domain covers the full loan lifecycle: lead intake, application assessment, settlement, loan servicing, and payments and collections, including single and recurring direct debits.

title: Architecture and system design experience
text: At Fsoft Huining designed and owned the architecture of a modular, domain-driven platform: cleanly separated bounded contexts on .NET, CQRS with MediatR, an asynchronous messaging backbone on Azure Service Bus for cross-component workflows, and independently deployable services and background workers. He works with event-driven patterns, message queues with retries and dead-letter handling, idempotent side effects, ports-and-adapters abstractions for third-party providers, and multi-tenant data isolation. He has deliberately traded distributed autonomy for strong consistency where regulated money movement demands it, and can explain that trade-off in depth.

title: Reliability, deployment and infrastructure-as-code
text: At Fsoft Huining designed a zero-downtime, fault-tolerant deployment strategy: blue/green releases behind Azure Front Door, stateless services with shared state in Redis and Key Vault, high-availability database failover, and expand-then-contract database migrations so old and new application versions can run against one database during rollout. He defined the Azure infrastructure as code in Microsoft Bicep (App Services, database, Service Bus, Key Vault, Azure AI Search, Functions, Storage, Application Insights, AD B2C and Container Apps) and connected it to CI/CD, replacing a manual runbook process with idempotent, repeatable multi-environment provisioning. He works with CI/CD in Azure DevOps and GitHub Actions, Docker, and observability through Application Insights.

title: AI engineering work in production
text: At Fsoft Huining built and shipped a Node.js/TypeScript Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) service over the platform's knowledge base and support-centre content, using LangChain, LangGraph, Azure OpenAI and Azure AI Foundry. It is exposed through internal and external MCP (Model Context Protocol) endpoints so AI assistants can query it directly. Answers carry source citations, the service refuses when relevant evidence is unavailable, and consequential actions sit behind human-in-the-loop controls. He added a live in-product chat widget built on the same retrieval service. He also led an AI-powered customer-matching solution using Azure AI Search, from architecture through production delivery. He works across models from multiple vendors (Anthropic, OpenAI and Azure OpenAI) and designs model-agnostic abstractions.

title: AI across the software delivery lifecycle
text: At Fsoft Huining introduced Claude Code and Codex to his team with written conventions, automated checks and code review, making agentic coding tools a core part of how the team shipped software. That included AI-assisted test generation, debugging and code review, plus agent guidance files, skills, hooks and reference implementations that let engineers use AI productively without lowering quality. He set the standards and guardrails for safe internal AI use, and treats verifying AI output as a first-class engineering skill rather than trusting it. He builds ShuttleRise the same way: the product is developed with AI coding agents (Claude Code and Codex) under his direction, while he owns product direction, architecture and quality controls.

text: Languages and frameworks: C#, .NET 8, ASP.NET Core, Entity Framework Core, Dapper, TypeScript, Angular (through Angular 20+ with signals), Node.js/Express, React (approximately 7 years of project experience, though Angular is his deepest commercial frontend experience), Python and SQL. Cloud and delivery: Microsoft Azure (App Service, Functions, Container Apps, Front Door, Service Bus, Key Vault, Blob Storage, AD B2C, Application Insights), Bicep, Docker, Azure DevOps and GitHub Actions, with working AWS exposure. Data: SQL Server, PostgreSQL and Redis. Architecture: REST APIs, event-driven systems, domain-driven design, CQRS with MediatR. Testing: xUnit, Moq, FluentAssertions and test-driven development.

title: AI and machine learning skills
text: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), embeddings and vector search, hybrid and semantic retrieval, chunking strategies, grounding and source citations. MCP servers, LangChain and LangGraph, multi-agent orchestration, tool use and structured output. Azure AI Search, Azure OpenAI and Azure AI Foundry. AI coding agents: Claude Code and Codex, including agent guidance (AGENTS.md), skill authoring, hooks and persistent agent memory. Responsible AI practice: input guardrails and prompt-injection screening, output validation, human-in-the-loop approval gates, explainability and audit trails. Evaluation: golden test sets, offline evals in CI, groundedness and citation-precision metrics, LLM-as-judge with human calibration, drift and quality monitoring.

title: Leadership and communication
text: At Fsoft Huining led a team of six engineers while remaining 40-50% hands-on. He set architecture and technical direction, reviewed designs and code, ran Agile ceremonies (stand-ups, sprint planning, retrospectives and brown-bag sessions), mentored engineers through code review, design review and pairing, and conducted performance reviews. He runs architecture decisions collaboratively, welcoming technical debate rather than mandating. He translates technical trade-offs into plain business language for senior and non-technical stakeholders up to executive level, and led cross-cutting initiatives that needed organisation-wide buy-in, such as the .NET 8 migration, the Angular 20+ migration and AI adoption. He works well where requirements are ambiguous and priorities shift, and prefers to bring structure to ambiguity rather than wait for perfect specifications.

title: Earlier career (2012 to 2020)
text: Before Fsoft, Huining worked as a Senior Software Engineer at three Brisbane organisations. At 1ICT Pty Ltd, an IT professional-services consultancy (January 2020 to July 2020), he delivered a COVID-19 desk-booking system for Domino's in four weeks, an e-commerce ordering portal, and OCR and Elasticsearch enhancements to ANZ's Marvin document system. At Sonic Healthcare (January 2019 to December 2019) he built clinic-management, patient kiosk and online booking applications deployed across hundreds of clinics nationwide. At Hastings Deering (July 2012 to December 2018) he developed enterprise applications including Asset Tracker, the HDEC catalogue and a SharePoint intranet, plus reporting in SSRS and Power BI.
